Mr. Vivek Sharma, Panel Lawyer for the State/respondent.
Heard on I.A. No.01/2023, which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.

By the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence dated 16-12-2022 passed in Sessions Trial/POCSO Case No.34/2019 by the learned Additional Sessions Judge/Fast Track Special Court (POCSO), District Kondagaon (C.G.) the appellant has been convicted under Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (in short 'the POCSO Act') and under Section 376 of the IPC and sentenced in the following manner :-
 Conviction Sentence  U/s 6 of the POCSO Act Rigorous Imprisonment for  and fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default of  payment of fine further R.I. for 3  months

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the prosecutrix was having love affair with the appellant and she was a consenting party in the alleged act of physical relation.

From the evidence of the prosecutrix, it clearly reflects that she has not raised any alarm and she developed physical relation with the appellant, it is only when she got pregnant, under the pressure of her parents she lodged the report.
During the trial the appellant was on bail and he has not misused the liberty so granted.
From the date of judgment, i.e., 16-12-2022 he is in jail and final adjudication of the appeal will take its own time, therefore, the appellant may be enlarged on bail.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the submission made by learned counsel for the appellant and has submitted that the appellant has developed physical relation with the prosecutrix by which she got pregnant and he ultimately refused to marry with her.
He would also submit that in the evidence of PW-2, mother of the prosecutrix it has come that the appellant was already married, yet he has developed physical relation with the prosecutrix.
He would further submit that the DNA test is also found to be positive that the appellant is biological father of the child of the prosecutrix.
Therefore, he is not entitled for bail.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the trial Court.

Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and further considering the nature of evidence available in the present case and considering the evidence of the prosecutrix (PW-1) as well as the DNA report in which the appellant is found to be biological father of the child of the prosecutrix, I am not inclined to release the appellant on bail.
Accordingly, I.A. No.01/2023, application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail is rejected.
List this case for final hearing after eight weeks.

Sd/-
(Ravindra Kumar Agrawal) Judge Aadil Bajman @ Rohan Netam vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176846257/
